clippings.speaker: Wes Anderson
clippings.quote: And then when I met him I thought that he had all kinds of things that we could sort of draw on for the character and kind of tap into. Like he'd never played -- he never had a family in a movie before. And he's got five kids and he's been a father for 17 years or something.
clippings.title: Film Director and Writer Wes Anderson
clippings.context: Anderson tells Terry Gross how he and Owen Wilson wrote the part of Mr. Blume with Murray in mind.

clippings.speaker: Wes Anderson
clippings.quote: He's a very physical guy, a very physical actor. … He might not have the build of a 'Die Hard'-era Bruce Willis, but he has the same desire. And I was always excited by the idea of him doing a shootout in a Speedo, robe and flip-flops.
clippings.film: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
clippings.title: Murray was a fish out of water making 'The Life Aquatic'
clippings.context: Anderson on casting Murray as Steve Zissou, quoted in a Newhouse profile of the film's release.

clippings.speaker: Wes Anderson
clippings.quote: My experience with Bill is so extensive. Bill was such a great supporter of me from the very beginning … he's really part of my family. You know, he's my daughter's godfather. In fact, he actually baptized her. He's the one who splashed the water.
clippings.title: Wes Anderson Stands by Bill Murray Amid Misconduct Claims: 'He Is Really Part of My Family'
clippings.context: Anderson, interviewed ahead of Asteroid City, on his bond with Murray after misconduct allegations against the actor.

clippings.speaker: Bill Murray
clippings.quote: When I read Rushmore, I figured the writing was so specific that whoever wrote it knew exactly what they were going to shoot. I never have a problem with guys who make a movie that misses as long as they make the movie they want to make. That's usually the hard part.
clippings.title: New Again: Bill Murray
clippings.context: Murray answers Anderson's questions in a joint conversation for Interview magazine (reprinted 2014; the reprint says it first ran in the February 2000 issue).

clippings.speaker: Bill Murray
clippings.quote: I sure as hell wouldn't leave the country and go over there with (just) anybody. You gotta have some faith in who you're with.
clippings.film: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
clippings.title: Murray's confidence in director led him to do 'Life Aquatic'
clippings.context: Murray at a New York press conference explaining why he trusted Anderson enough to shoot in Italy.

clippings.speaker: Bill Murray
clippings.quote: He was just a kid, but he was also a guy who knew what the hell he was doing and what he wanted to do, right from the beginning. … We had a good relationship, I felt like I was looking out for him and I still am. I like him, he's my friend.
clippings.title: Bill Murray: "It's more intake than output"
clippings.context: Murray recalls meeting Anderson in Houston on the Rushmore shoot; the two parts are answers to consecutive questions.

notes: Rolling Stone (tollbit redirect) and Texas Monthly (403) were blocked and skipped; the Interview piece is dated 1999 from a search snippet and Rushmore Academy listing, while the reprint says February 2000.
